definitions.statement: The selected six-face distributions are yellow [3,3,3,3,3,3], blue [4,4,4,4,0,0], green [1,1,1,5,5,5], and orange [2,2,2,2,6,6].
definitions.caveat: Exact same selected configuration and color mapping; repeated labels are distinct equally likely faces. Index order is not a physical cube net.

definitions.statement: In this two-player model, each player selects a different die, rolls once independently, and the higher number wins.
definitions.caveat: Not a sum-of-rolls game or arbitrary altered rules. An illustrative outcome is not sampled empirical evidence.

definitions.statement: The calculations assume six equally likely faces per die and independent rolls, so each indexed face pair has probability 1/36.
definitions.caveat: Mathematical model assumptions, not measured fairness of physical dice or a guarantee from a physics simulation.

definitions.statement: Two independent six-face dice with equally likely faces give 36 equally likely indexed face-pair outcomes.
definitions.caveat: Derived as6×6; repeated displayed values must not be deduplicated or assigned equal weight to value types.

definitions.statement: Yellow has probability 2/3 of beating orange: its constant3 beats the four2 faces and loses to the two6 faces, giving24 wins out of36 indexed pairs.
definitions.caveat: Strictly greater, independent equal-face model. Chance result, not a guaranteed individual or finite-series outcome.

definitions.statement: Blue has probability 2/3 of beating yellow: four4 faces beat3 while two0 faces lose, giving24 wins out of36 indexed pairs.
definitions.caveat: Same exact model; no claim that blue beats every opponent2/3 of the time.

definitions.statement: Green has probability 2/3 of beating blue: its three5 faces produce18 winning pairs against all blue faces, and its three1 faces produce6 further winning pairs against blue’s two0 faces, giving24 of36.
definitions.caveat: Add disjoint branches:1/2+(1/2×1/3)=2/3. Do not imply that all four value-type combinations are equally likely.

definitions.statement: Orange has probability 2/3 of beating green: its two6 faces produce12 winning pairs against all green faces, and its four2 faces produce12 further winning pairs against green’s three1 faces, giving24 of36.
definitions.caveat: Add disjoint branches:1/3+(2/3×1/2)=2/3. Every2-versus5 pair loses.

definitions.statement: The four specified advantages form the cycle yellow over orange, blue over yellow, green over blue, and orange over green, each with probability2/3.
definitions.caveat: An arrow means pairwise probability advantage, not guaranteed victory. Only these neighboring cycle matchups have2/3.

definitions.statement: After any first choice in this set, an informed second player can select a remaining die that has probability2/3 of beating it under the model.
definitions.caveat: Information and counter-choice are essential; selecting second randomly does not confer this strategy. No gambling or financial advice.

definitions.statement: Every specified favorable2/3 matchup still has12 losing face pairs out of36; either player can win an individual roll.
definitions.caveat: A single possible loss does not refute the probability result. Finite series need not show a2:1 ratio.

definitions.statement: No die in this selected set is more likely to beat every other die; which die has favorable odds depends on the opponent.
definitions.caveat: Pairwise distributions can be nontransitive; actual realized numbers retain ordinary transitive ordering. No universal claim about all rankings.

definitions.statement: No two distinct dice in this selected configuration can tie in a single roll because their sets of face labels are disjoint.
definitions.caveat: Different Efron sets can have ties; MathWorld’s separate reroll variant is not this configuration.

definitions.statement: Nontransitivity here concerns the relation P(X>Y)>1/2 between dice, not greater-than between individual realized numbers.
definitions.caveat: Precise mathematical concept; terminology intentionally not required in the spoken script.

definitions.statement: Orange against blue has probability5/9=20/36 of winning in the selected independent equal-face model.
definitions.caveat: Derived from exact source face labels and fully enumerated; not a cycle edge or another2/3 claim.

definitions.statement: Yellow against green has probability1/2=18/36 of winning in the selected independent equal-face model.
definitions.caveat: Equal win probabilities are not ties in realized numbers; every roll still produces a strict winner.

definitions.statement: A separate Efron dice variant has ties and a reroll rule, unlike this selected set.
definitions.caveat: Reference prose inspected; its image labels not inspected. No imported alternate set or odds claim.

definitions.statement: Choosing second guarantees winning every roll.
definitions.caveat: Excluded: each favorable edge still has12 losing face pairs.

definitions.statement: Every distinct pairing in the four-die set gives one player a2/3 win probability.
definitions.caveat: Excluded: opposite pairings are5/9 and1/2, not2/3.

definitions.statement: A realized3 can beat a realized6 under the higher-number-wins rule.
definitions.caveat: Excluded:3<6. Yellow outperforms the2/6 distribution, not the outcome6.

definitions.statement: A favorable die must win exactly six of nine rolls.
definitions.caveat: Excluded: probability is not a guaranteed finite frequency. No series performed.

definitions.statement: The paradox requires physically loaded dice.
definitions.caveat: Excluded: the equal-face model already demonstrates the complete result.

definitions.statement: Physical specimens of these dice have been experimentally demonstrated to give equiprobable faces.
definitions.caveat: Unresolved and unselected: no physical specimens or experiment acquired. Model assumption is retained explicitly.
